Formulation
- Predisposing factors: family history of migraine (mother).
- Precipitating factors: acute onset left-sided headache with visual disturbance, nausea, vomiting beginning this morning.
- Perpetuating factors: ongoing anxiety about serious illness, limited response to initial paracetamol, avoidance of movement/screens due to symptoms.
- Protective factors: patient sought medical attention promptly, receptive to conservative acute treatment and follow-up; no focal neurological deficits reported in history or on remote assessment.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Probable migraine (acute left-sided headache with visual disturbance)
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Rapid relief of headache, visual symptoms and nausea.
  - Reassurance and avoidance of serious underlying pathology.
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Provide acute symptom relief.
  - Reassess and perform full neurological examination if symptoms persist or worsen; exclude serious intracranial pathology.
- Actions (Patient):
  - Obtain and take recommended OTC ibuprofen and an antiemetic from pharmacy (medication names/doses not documented).
  - Drink fluids and consider a sugary/carbonated drink (e.g., Coke) as advised.
  - Rest, avoid screens and minimize head movement.
  - Attend same-day clinic review as offered, or cancel appointment if symptoms resolve.
  - Seek immediate emergency care if new focal neurological signs, worsening headache, loss of consciousness, or severe deterioration occur.
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Advise trial of ibuprofen plus an anti-sickness medication (names/doses not documented) and symptomatic measures (hydration, sugary/carbonated drink, rest).
  - Offer same-day clinical review with full neurological examination.
  - Escalate to urgent imaging/ED assessment if focal neurological deficits or clinical deterioration occur.

Secondary Problem: Concern for intracranial pathology (patient-identified)
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Reassurance and appropriate investigation if indicated.
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Identify or exclude focal neurological signs; ensure timely escalation if red flags present.
- Actions (Patient):
  - Monitor for new symptoms: weakness, slurred speech, facial droop, worsening vision, altered consciousness.
  - Present to ED immediately if any of these occur.
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Perform neurological exam at same-day review.
  - Arrange urgent imaging/referral or ED transfer if exam or symptom progression indicates.

Tertiary Problem: Health anxiety / hypochondriasis (self-described)
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Reduce persistent excessive worry about health.
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Provide education and reassurance; consider referral for psychological support if anxiety persists.
- Actions (Patient):
  - Discuss ongoing concerns at follow-up appointment.
  - Consider acceptance of referral to mental health services if recommended.
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Provide education about migraine and expected course.
  - Offer follow-up to review symptoms and consider referral to mental health services if health anxiety remains problematic.

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered:
  - Migraine features and typical course (can last 4–72 hours).
  - Acute self-management: NSAID (ibuprofen) + antiemetic, hydration, sugary/carbonated drink (e.g., Coke), rest/avoid screens.
  - When to seek urgent care (new focal neurology, severe or worsening symptoms).
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening:
  - New focal neurological deficits (weakness, speech disturbance), increasing severity or frequency of headache, persistent uncontrollable vomiting, decreased consciousness.
- Coping Strategies:
  - Rest in a dark, quiet environment, keep head still, avoid screens, use pharmacy analgesia/antiemetic as advised, contact clinic or ED if worsens.

Consent, Coordination & Review
- Patient Consent to Plan: Yes (patient agreed to recommendations and follow-up).
- Copy of Mental Health Care Plan Given to Patient: Not recorded.
- Other Mental Health Professionals Involved in Patient Care: Not recorded.
- GP Acknowledgment (if completed by other MH Professional): Not recorded.
- Review Date: Same-day review offered; exact appointment time/date not documented.

Quality checks
● Missing but clinically expected elements: documented formal neurological examination findings, vital signs, medication doses/routes/frequencies, confirmed diagnosis, comprehensive past medical/psychiatric history, risk level for self-harm, emergency contact details, exact follow-up time/date.  
● Internal conflicts from the transcript: clinician said "hyperthyroid" while patient stated her mother has "hypothyroidism" — conflict noted.  
● Transcript quality notes: brief telemedicine connection interruption reported by clinician and patient; some speech portions slightly unclear.
